english.title: Possess article for purposes of terrorism - Terrorism Act 2000
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), possessed an article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), in circumstances which gave rise to a reasonable suspicion that your possession was for a purpose connected with the commission, preparation or instigation of an act of terrorism
english.legislation: Contrary to section 57(1) and (4) of the Terrorism Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
possess articles(s) in suspicious circumstances
purpose the commission/preparation of acts of terrorism

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required
(ii) See Section 57(2) for defence
(iii) See Section 1 for an interpretation of 'terrorism'.
(iv) Section 13 of the Terrorism Act 2006 increased the maximum penalty from 10 to 15 years for offences committed AFTER 13th April 2006.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fifteen years imprisonment and / or a fine. For offences committed before 13th April 2006: ten years imprisonment and / or fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
